inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 31 March 2026: 827.503m allotted less 4.694m own shares (4.412m treasury + 0.282m ESOT) = 822.8m outstanding, plus 2.4m dilutive awards (diluted 862.67m vs basic 860.24m weighted, FY2026 AR note 10) = 825.2m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the FY2027 c.GBP500m buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral in this model (accretive only to the extent shares are bought below IV). Post-balance-sheet buybacks (c.8m shares by 21 May 2026, more since) and the matching RCF draw are both excluded so shares and net debt share one vintage.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report: share-based payments charge excluding associated NI GBP9.2m (note 29, line 7635); share-based payments including employer NI GBP9.7m (financial review people-cost table, line 1610). Employer NI on awards is the UK analogue of equity-award cash taxes, so the GBP9.7m combined figure is used. FY2027 guided at GBP14m.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts GBP/share to pence/share (model -> quote). No currency risk and no dual listing: parity is exact by definition. Any IV within two orders of magnitude of 4.6 rather than 460 is the pounds-vs-pence bug, not a valuation view.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:36:31Z (LSE closing auction, Friday; regular close, not after-hours)
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-built: UK 10y gilt ~4.5%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.05 (de-rated UK marketplace) gives cost of equity ~9.75%; after-tax cost of debt ~4% (SONIA + 1.2-2.1% margin on the Syndicated RCF, 25% tax); target leverage c.1.0x EBITDA (~10% of EV) gives WACC ~9.2%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows (scenario paths and weights), not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Lease liabilities GBP42.6m (new Manchester HQ lease from June 2025, note 14) are included in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Chosen because the HQ lease is rent-free until April 2028, so FY2026 cash lease payments (GBP1.8m principal) badly understate the ongoing cost and treatment (B) would flatter the next two years. Right-of-use depreciation (GBP4.7m) stays inside D&A and is added back; lease-asset renewal is carried as a capex-like charge by ramping capex_pct from 0.8% to 1.5% of revenue so the terminal year bears an economic rent.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no non-controlling interests. Dealer Auction is a 50% JV whose share of profit (GBP4.1m) sits inside operating profit and EBITDA; it is left in the flows (JV distributions broadly match) and no bridge item is added, which slightly flatters FCF by at most ~1%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md routing table, operating company / marketplace). Auto Trader is the UK's dominant automotive classifieds marketplace: subscription revenue from ~13.9k retailer forecourts (ARPR GBP2,995/month), 70% segment operating margin, negligible capex, FCF conversion >90% of net income. Not a bank, REIT or holdco; an owner-FCF DCF is the right engine. EBITDA BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC (adjusted) EBITDA. FY2026 statutory EBITDA 416.1 (operating profit 392.7 + D&A 23.4) is after the GBP9.7m SBC expense, so the pre-SBC margin is (416.1 + 9.7) / 624.3 = 68.2%; the engine's own SBC deduction then returns EBIT = statutory operating profit (FY2027 base EBIT ~GBP402m ties to the GBP395-415m guidance). ONE-OFF CAPEX: FY2026 PPE purchases of GBP27.3m include GBP25.1m HQ fit-out (note 13); normal capex is GBP4-5m (0.7% of revenue). last_fcf (285.7) is the reported figure less SBC and is depressed by ~GBP23m of that one-off; the forward capex_pct path is normalised at 0.8%. HQ sale proceeds of GBP4.5m are excluded from reported_fcf. INTEREST INCOME: GBP0.3m on a net-debt balance sheet, immaterial, set to 0. TAX: UK statutory 25%; FY2026 cash tax GBP95.2m on PBT GBP388.8m = 24.5%, so a flat 25% cash rate is used (modelled tax on EBIT 392.7 x 25% = 98.2 vs 95.2 paid, within non-deductible Autorama amortisation noise). WORKING CAPITAL: 0% capture; retailers pay monthly by direct debit (89.7%), there is no material deferred-revenue tailwind, and Autorama's temporary vehicle stocking is small. GUIDANCE ANCHOR (FY2027, 21 May 2026): Group operating profit GBP395-415m; Autotrader revenue flat in April 2026, growth in H2; ARPR price lever +GBP85-95, product +GBP65-75, stock -GBP30-40; average forecourts -1-2%; other revenue flat; Autorama small profit, Commission & Ancillary +8-12%, Vehicle & Accessory sales c.GBP40m; SBC GBP14m; Autorama amortisation GBP13.0m; marketing to increase; c.GBP500m buyback plus one-third of net income as dividends (c.GBP600m total), leverage to c.1.0x. PRICE RATIOS (pence vs pounds checked): market cap 825.2m x GBP4.617 = GBP3.81bn; EV ~GBP4.0bn; EV/statutory EBITDA 9.6x; P/E 13.5x on diluted EPS 34.07p; owner-FCF yield ~7.5% on normalised FY2026 owner FCF (~GBP309m ex HQ one-off). The stock fell from 828.8p to 461.7p inside the 52-week range on the Deal Builder retailer backlash (Nov 2025) and AI/Amazon Autos disintermediation fears.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case average revenue growth FY2027-FY2031. Equity CAGR is negative because buybacks (GBP369m FY2026) exceed earnings, so the usual equity anchor is unusable for a capital-returning company; revenue 3yr CAGR 7.7% overstates the near term given FY2027 guidance of roughly flat H1 revenue and +1% to +6% operating profit.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-8.3% 3yr) diverges from revenue (+7.7%) and EPS (+11.2%) by far more than 30%: shareholders' equity fell from GBP527m to GBP407m because cumulative buybacks and dividends (GBP989m over FY2024-FY2026) exceeded cumulative net income (GBP833m). Book value is not a meaningful growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: All 5yr CAGRs run from FY2021 (year to March 2021), which was depressed by COVID free-advertising months (revenue GBP263m vs GBP369m in FY2020), so they overstate trend growth; the 6yr CAGR from FY2020 is 9.2% for revenue. FCF series is owner FCF (reported FCF less the CSV's SBC charge; interest income immaterial throughout): FY2021 120.0, FY2022 264.0, FY2023 257.7, FY2024 276.2, FY2025 290.9, FY2026 286.2. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (3.6%) is below reported (3.9%): SBC grew 16%/yr vs FCF 4%, so a rising share of growth is paid in stock, though SBC is still only ~1.5% of revenue. FY2026 owner FCF is also depressed by the GBP23m HQ fit-out one-off; ex that the 3yr owner-FCF CAGR would be ~6.5%, in line with EBIT growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +3.5%: retailer revenue ~+2.5% (ARPR +~GBP125 net of stock drag on 2,995 = +4%, forecourts -1.5%), other revenue flat, Autorama +~GBP11m on Vehicle & Accessory sales; flat H1 per guidance. FY2028-FY2030 recover to 4.5-5% as the Deal Builder relationship normalises and the April pricing event resumes its ~GBP100+/yr ARPR cadence with forecourts stable. Decelerates to 2.5% by FY2036 as the retailer base is mature and UK transactions plateau near ~10m.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 68.2% FY2026 -> 68.5% FY2027 (operating profit guidance midpoint GBP405m + D&A ~GBP26.5m + SBC GBP14m on revenue ~GBP646m = 68.9%; held slightly lower for the guided marketing increase and 1-2% of low-margin Autorama vehicle sales growth). Drifts to 69.5% by FY2031 as revenue outgrows a largely fixed cost base; management guides margins 'at least maintained'. No return to the 72% of FY2020 is assumed.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 4.1% in FY2027 (Autorama acquired-intangible amortisation GBP13m, full-year HQ ROU depreciation and fit-out depreciation) runs off to 2.0% as the acquired intangibles are fully amortised by ~FY2032. Capex 0.8% (GBP4-5m normal run-rate) ramps to 1.5% so that by the terminal year the flows carry lease-asset renewal under lease treatment (A).

bull.narrative: Top of FY2027 guidance (operating profit ~GBP415m) as forecourts stop shrinking by H2; Deal Builder (6.7k retailers, 137k reservations) and Buying Signals convert into a transactional product lever worth GBP100+/yr of ARPR on top of price; data/API monetisation (155m calls/month) and new-car/leasing add a second growth engine; AI assistants route via Autotrader's MCP/ChatGPT integrations rather than around it, so direct traffic (>80% of visits) holds. Revenue grows 6-7% FY2028-FY2030 and margins expand to 71.5% on operating leverage, close to the FY2020 peak.

bear.narrative: Bottom of FY2027 guidance (operating profit ~GBP395m), then Amazon Autos' UK launch and agentic AI search give retailers a credible second channel: the April pricing event is diluted, forecourts fall 2-3%/yr through FY2030, paid stock and package penetration slip, and marketing is raised to defend audience. Revenue declines 1-2%/yr in FY2028-FY2030 and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses to 63% before stabilising at ~1.5% growth. This is deliberately milder than the Board's viability stress (10% of retailers lost in FY2027, Trade revenue -25% over two years) because that scenario is a solvency test, not a central downside; the business survives it with >GBP200m of FCF.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 Deal Builder backlash (up to ~460 retailers left at the peak, forecourts -0.5%, employee engagement 91% -> 72%) is a relationship wound that heals rather than a structural break: FY2027 lands near the GBP405m operating-profit midpoint with flat H1 revenue and H2 recovery, then the annual pricing-and-product event resumes delivering ARPR growth of ~4-5%/yr against a stable ~13.5-14k forecourt base. Autotrader keeps >80% direct traffic and 6x the engagement of all competitors combined, so AI assistants and Amazon Autos erode growth at the margin rather than displacing the marketplace. Margins drift up ~1pp; SBC settles at ~2% of revenue; capex stays <1.5%. The c.GBP500m FY2027 buyback is value-neutral in the model but, executed at ~13x earnings, is accretive to the per-share value of a buyer today.
scenario_narratives.bull: Retailer sentiment recovers fully by H2 FY2027, Deal Builder and Buying Signals become a paid transactional layer, data/API and new-car/leasing revenue scale, and AI becomes a distribution channel Autotrader sits inside rather than a bypass. Revenue growth 6-7% in FY2028-FY2030 and pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~71.5% by FY2032; the market re-rates back toward the historical 20x+ earnings multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Amazon Autos UK and LLM-driven discovery give retailers pricing leverage for the first time: forecourts and paid stock decline for three years, ARPR growth turns negative, marketing spend rises, and margins compress ~5pp to 63%. The balance sheet is being levered to ~1.0x EBITDA for buybacks at the same time, so the equity bears more of any earnings miss. Revenue troughs ~4% below FY2026 and grows only 1.5% thereafter.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the downside axis is structural and already partly observed: retailers demonstrably reduced stock and left the platform when pushed in FY2026, management itself says AI will change how many users begin their research, a well-capitalised entrant (Amazon Autos) is expected in the UK in 2026, and the balance sheet is being levered into that uncertainty. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: forecourt recovery, a successful transactional (Deal Builder) monetisation that retailers just rejected in its mandatory form, and AI acting as a channel rather than a bypass. Base at 50%: the two-sided network, >80% direct traffic and subscription model make continued low-to-mid single digit ARPR-led growth the central case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Auto Trader is valued as a mature, near-monopoly UK marketplace whose owner FCF (~GBP300m normalised, >90% of net income) grows with ARPR rather than audience. The valuation hinges on whether the FY2026 retailer backlash and AI/Amazon disintermediation fears mark a permanent loss of pricing power (bear) or a one-year wound in an intact flywheel (base). SBC is fully expensed and the share count held flat; leases sit in net debt; cash tax is the 25% UK statutory rate; the terminal value is Gordon at 2.5% growth, well inside the 18x FCF cap.
key_risks_to_valuation: Agentic AI / LLM search and Amazon Autos UK disintermediating retailer prominence revenue, which is the whole of the price and product ARPR levers
Retailer forecourt attrition continuing beyond the guided 1-2% for FY2027 after the Deal Builder episode showed the limits of pricing power
Leverage rising to ~1.0x EBITDA for buybacks: value-neutral in the model, but the equity now carries ~GBP400-600m of debt into any downside
Regulatory: CMA online-reviews investigation, FCA motor-finance redress affecting retailer financial health, UK Digital Services Tax (GBP10.6m) rising
Terminal value is ~55-60% of EV at a 9% WACC; each 1pp of WACC moves base IV by roughly 15%
